articleTitle: The impact of ATM networks on video coding
abstract: As the CCITT SGXVIII has decided on the asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) as the target technique to implement B-ISDN, it becomes necessary to study the impact of this technique on video coding. The following ATM issues affect video coding: standardisation, variable bit rate coding, cell loss, synchronisation, user selectable picture quality, and multiplexing of service components. An overview of these issues is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The transmission of variable bit rate video over an Orwell Ring
abstract: Future broadband ISDNs are likely to be based on a new transfer technique known as asynchronous transfer mode (ATM). The emergence of these broadband ATM networks will bring about new concepts in providing telecommunication services, such as a real-time variable bit rate (VBR) connection. Supporting VBR video on an ATM network however raises a number of traffic control problems, especially in a multiservices environment. For example, VBR video cannot be allowed to cause cell loss on the CBO services, and at the same time VBR video must be protected against excessive cell loss. This protection must not be at the expense of bandwidth utilisation efficiency, otherwise the gain of VBR video will be nullified. These issues are addressed carefully particularly in relation to an ATM network known as the Orwell Ring.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of ATM protocols for video services
abstract: Asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) operation has now been recognised as a basis for a multiservice network that will permit broadband operation up to a high bit rate. The CCITT Study Group XVIII has made some progress towards the definition of such a network but much remains to be done before complete Recommendations can be produced and viable systems implemented. The main problem is that, although the broadband ISDN network will provide a (digital) bearer service, it cannot be defined in isolation. The teleservices to be carried on the B-ISDN need to be considered in relation to both the interfacing to the bearer network and the effects of impairments produced by the network. Interest has been concentrated on both interactive and distributive video services because they are likely to constitute a major source of traffic for the B-ISDN. An attempt has been made to model conditional replenishment coded video signals carried over an ATM network under a range of traffic loadings and so characterise the impairments to the teleservices that would be produced by the bearer network. This information can then be used to assess the human factors perception of the video services that might be carried by the network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterisation of video and generation of statistically equivalent Markov modulated Poisson processes
abstract: Determines the cell interarrival time distribution of a video codec, a number of these sources are then superposed into an aggregate cell arrival process and this stream is finally approximated to a statistically equivalent Markov Modulated Poisson Process (MMPP). The MMPP representations of video sources can then be superposed to generate composite sources. The motivation for generating an equivalent MMPP is to facilitate theoretical analysis of queueing systems performance and for generating composite sources for simulation studies. Theoretical analysis of queueing systems performance is important since it yields important measures of cell loss and transfer time at the extreme ends of their distributions. This work uses the techniques of Heffes and Lucantoni (1986).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Two-component video coding for packet networks
abstract: Two-component coding of video signals based on conditional replenishment (CR) for packet networks is described. The type of network is assumed to be an Orwell slotted ring, where transmission of certain packets is guaranteed. The coder produces two component bit streams; the first bit stream contains all the important structural information of the conditionally replenished video data and is accommodated in the guaranteed capacity of the network. The second output is transmitted through the variable bit rate (VBR) channel of the network, which if received improves picture quality. Using CIF standard pictures, the performance of the coder is compared with that of the conventional CR coder for various packet loss rates.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Video transmission over variable bit rate networks
abstract: Highlights the problems associated with transmitting compressed video over a synchronous network and the possible advantages of transporting this data over an asynchronous network. A description is included of experimental work being carried out to investigate the requirements of transmitting video over a variable bit rate network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
